purpose: Tizanidine is used to relieve muscle spasms and tightness, often caused by conditions like multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injuries. It helps your muscles relax so you can move more comfortably and with less pain. Doctors may also prescribe it for other conditions involving muscle stiffness.
how_it_works: Tizanidine works by sending calming signals in your brain and spinal cord that tell your muscles to relax. Think of it like turning down the volume on the signals that are making your muscles tense up and spasm. This helps reduce the tightness and discomfort in your muscles without completely blocking normal movement.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or sleepiness is very common, so be careful driving or using machinery. You may also feel dizzy, especially when standing up quickly. Other common effects include dry mouth, weakness, and low blood pressure. Some people notice their liver enzymes go up, so your doctor may check blood tests.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as it can cause withdrawal symptoms like high blood pressure and a fast heartbeat. Avoid alcohol while taking tizanidine because it can make drowsiness much worse. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially blood pressure drugs or fluvoxamine, as dangerous interactions can occur. Tizanidine can also affect your liver, so let your doctor know if you have any liver problems.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 2 mg taken by mouth every 6 to 8 hours as needed for muscle spasms. Your doctor may slowly increase the dose up to a maximum of 36 mg per day. Take only as many doses as your doctor prescribes, and try not to miss doses or double up if you forget one.
